testcase.name: working -> idle -> blocked -> none: each confirmed transition is exactly one Jira update
herdr's agent_status flickering within the stabilization window produces zero label churn
a genuinely stable transition (new status held for 2 consecutive polls) still produces exactly one add/remove pair
human labels are never added or removed, and survive reconciliation
no-change poll -> zero Jira writes
a ticket that leaves the active set (disappears from the feed) has all agent:* removed
a ticket's human labels are never re-added when it disappears from the feed (regression)
a ticket seen directly with a non-active status (not merely disappeared) also has agent:* cleared
pr:* is independently reconciled and untouched by the active-leave cleanup
restart durability: an active ticket already carrying pr:merged, whose PR is confirmed merged again after a cold-cache rediscovery, gets zero label writes (no remove/re-add cycle)
an 'unknown' lookup on a ticket carrying pr:merged issues zero updateLabels calls
a genuine null prState (confirmed no PR / closed-unmerged) actually strips an existing pr:* label — case 2/9 guard
an Epic never triggers pr:* discovery (KAN-824): prState is never called for issuetype Epic
onPollEnd fires once per syncLabels run when supplied (KAN-824 poll boundary for PrTracker.endPoll)
pr:* disabled (no prState dep) never adds a pr:* label, agent:* unaffected
returns the set of keys written this poll
onWrite fires once with the written keys; not at all when nothing was written
done maps to agent:idle, not agent:working (herdr's done = sitting at its prompt)
a persistently failing write for one issue is isolated: other issues still get written, one log line, no throw
a failed write is not recorded as applied: the key is retried, not treated as already-labeled
stalled: takes precedence over idle, goes through the SAME 2-poll stabilizer as any other agent:* value
stalled is never applied when the observed status isn't idle, even if the check reports true
the stalled log line fires immediately (unlike the label, not delayed by the stabilizer)
the stalled log line includes elapsed minutes when the stalled dep exposes them
the stalled log line omits elapsed minutes gracefully when the stalled dep doesn't expose them (existing fixtures unaffected)
a stalled check that could not verify (null) never writes agent:stalled onto a ticket that wasn't already labelled stalled, even across two consecutive polls
REGRESSION: a stalled check that could not verify (null) never STRIPS an already-applied agent:stalled label, even across two consecutive polls
leaving the active set forgets the stalled tracker's state for that ticket
a permanently failing write logs 'write failed' exactly once, not once per poll; a change in reason logs again
a failing write on the disappearance-cleanup path is retried on a later poll instead of being dropped

FACTORY-502 (c): the dedupe map size is capped on insert — beyond the cap, further distinct keys are suppressed rather than growing the map
FACTORY-502 (d): a live key is never re-`set` — repeating it inside the window does not extend its own dedupe TTL
FACTORY-502 (d): the early-exit prune stops at the first unexpired entry without over- or under-pruning a live entry behind it

testcase.name: docs/rules.example.json: epics/stories/bugs migrate, tasks/subtasks do not
an `in (...)` list of only exempt types migrates
an `in (...)` list mixing an exempt and a non-exempt type does not migrate
quoted values and case-insensitivity both work
no issuetype clause at all: skip, cannot classify
more than one top-level issuetype clause: skip, ambiguous
negation (!=): skip — restriction only, never exclusion
negation (not in): skip
OR-combined with another clause: skip — an OR can widen what actually matches
issuetype clause nested inside an OR-containing parenthesized group is still safely classified at depth 0
unbalanced parens/quotes: skip, refuses to guess
a quoted string literal containing the word issuetype/order-by-like text is inert, never mistaken for a real clause
a trailing top-level ORDER BY does not stop an otherwise-clean issuetype clause from migrating
ORDER BY after an `in (...)` list also does not block migration
ORDER BY after a non-exempt issuetype still correctly skips (Task is not epic/story/bug)
jira-work rule with no role, exempt-only query: migrate

execution: reuses Rule's ExecutionMode enum verbatim, invalid value rejected
account: reuses Rule's AccountPolicy enum verbatim, invalid value rejected
role: reuses Rule's AgentRole enum verbatim (worker/sentinel), default worker, invalid value rejected
frozen: boolean, defaults false — a frozen definition is still a VALID one (validity and frozen-ness are independent axes)

testcase.name: state() before any mint: not minted, not locked, no expiry
mint() returns a 13-character code from the no-ambiguous-character base32 alphabet, and never 0/O/1/I/L
a correct code is accepted exactly once (single-use) — the second check against the same code fails
check() is case-insensitive
a wrong code decrements attempts; the 5th wrong attempt locks, after which even the correct code is refused until a fresh mint
null/undefined/non-string candidates are refused as a mismatch, never thrown, and still consume an attempt
a code expires after its TTL — check() reports expired, not mismatch, and state() clears
state() reports an ISO expiresAt while a code is live
mint() replaces a live code and resets attempts/lockout
mints a fresh code and logs exactly one line containing it on SIGUSR2; never writes it anywhere else
uninstalling removes the listener — a later SIGUSR2 does not log again
a valid file swaps the holder's rules and reports added/removed/changed
a rule present before and after, with a different query, is reported changed — never silently missed
disabling a previously-enabled rule reports it removed from the enabled set, even though the id is still present in the file
invalid JSON keeps the running rules untouched and reports the parse problem
a schema validation failure keeps the running rules untouched and reports the problem
a missing default file is a VALID reload to zero rules when the holder is ALREADY empty — nothing to wipe
review round 1, BLOCKING finding 1: a missing file over a NON-EMPTY holder is REFUSED, never swapped in — a vanished/moved/bad-mount rules file must not wipe every running rule
an explicit BUTCHR_RULES_FILE that does not exist is reported as a failed reload, keeping the running rules — same refusal, an explicit path
a PRESENT file that parses to zero rules IS accepted over a non-empty holder — an operator's deliberate 'disable everything' is distinguishable from a vanished file

not eligible on first observation
not eligible on a second observation before 60s of wall clock have passed
eligible once BOTH two observations AND >= 60s have elapsed
a third+ observation after eligibility keeps reporting eligible (still a candidate every later poll until reclaimed or it stops being one)
the counter resets when the workspace drops out of the candidate set in between (gained an agent, or disappeared) — a later reappearance starts over
independent ids are tracked independently

processInfo throwing is UNKNOWN, never dead — not reaped

every pane reports a non-claude foreground process (e.g. fish) — reaped
multiple panes, one live — the whole workspace is vetoed, not reaped

workspace.close itself rejecting is caught — resolves false, never throws
finds a workspace this process never spawned — ownership is read fresh from herdr state, not from in-memory bookkeeping

the grace period holds end to end: not reaped on the first poll, reaped once two polls and 60s have both passed
a candidate that gains an agent between polls (drops out of the candidate set) is never reaped, even though it later reappears
a live-but-unlisted agent is never reaped, this poll or any later poll, even once its grace period is long past
a failing close does not fail the poll, and does not prevent the other candidates from being closed
a candidates() gather failure degrades to reaped-nothing-this-poll — never throws
nothing eligible this poll → close is never called at all
release is called with the candidate's REAL agentKey after a successful close

runs journalctl with the unit's OWN derived argv, never a guessed one, bounded by -n
redacts a seeded secret in a log line — never returns it unredacted
bounded by byte cap: stops adding lines once the cap would be exceeded and reports truncated
log source failure (journalctl not available / timeout): operator-actionable error, not a throw
default bounds are sane (count and byte cap both finite and positive)
distro not installed -> wsl-down, exit 2, before anything else is even consulted
distro installed but not running -> wsl-down, exit 2
WSL up, systemd not active -> daemon-down, exit 1, headline distinguishes from wsl-down
WSL up, systemd state unknown (exec into distro failed) -> daemon-down, not silently healthy
systemd active, unit not active -> daemon-down, journal tail surfaced
unit active but /health unreachable -> daemon-down (unreachable treated as unhealthy, never assumed fine)
unit active, /health reachable but ok:false -> daemon-down
everything up and healthy -> healthy, exit 0
exit codes table matches what every branch above actually returns
(a) vs (b) is unmistakable: wsl-down headline never says daemon, daemon-down headline never says just DOWN alone

status

summary

testcase.name: tools and notifications share one connection, stable gateway authenticates and caches configuration
optional or invalid MCP configuration never silently connects another identity
empty registry + NOT ready + valid persisted token => 503 + Retry-After + JSON body
an agent retired BEFORE a restart (never prepared in the new instance) still gets 401 once the global startup deadline elapses — not 503 forever

FACTORY-700/702: an agent whose prepare() is still IN FLIGHT (not abandoned) when the global deadline elapses is HELD, not flipped to 401 — the cliff no longer fires for "slow", only for "never coming back"
wrong token, at any readiness, is 401
unknown agent / unknown name / no token file => 401, never 503, identical response to a wrong-token 401 (no existence leak)
READY + absent connection + valid persisted token => 401, not 503 (the retire path — retain() leaves the token file on disk)
path-traversal and reserved-name attempts in agent and name are 401 and touch nothing outside the workspace
GET with no Mcp-Session-Id => 405 (not 400), JSON body — the status the SDK client special-cases as "no SSE, carry on"
FACTORY-696/697/698 regression: a client holding its PRE-restart Mcp-Session-Id completes a real tools/call with no re-initialize, no 404, and an unchanged session id
rewriteSessionHeader: a post-adoption response carrying the PROXY-minted Mcp-Session-Id is rewritten to the client's own id
a malformed Mcp-Session-Id (not visible-ASCII, or over the length bound) is rejected with 400 JSON — never forwarded or adopted
DELETE for an unknown/stale Mcp-Session-Id is a pass-through, never triggers adoption (no pointless adopt-then-delete)
a successful DELETE drops the client-to-proxy session binding — clientToProxy does not grow forever
FACTORY-697 pre-review #4: clientToProxy is capped — the connection abandoned without a DELETE (the realistic restart case) still cannot grow the map without bound
concurrent requests for the same unknown/stale Mcp-Session-Id single-flight the gateway-initiated initialize — exactly one, not one per request
single-flight hole (FACTORY-697 pre-review #3): the clientToProxy binding is recorded BEFORE pending is cleared, so no request can see both empty
FACTORY-697 pre-review #1: a FAILING adoption (gateway-initiated initialize itself fails) is 503 + Retry-After, not a terminal 502 — mirrors the FACTORY-691 idiom
upstream genuinely down is passed straight through (JSON-ified), never adopted or masked as a session problem

FACTORY-702: a client modelled on the real ~8s retry budget (initial POST + 3 retries at 1s/2s/4s, THEN NOTHING MORE) still reaches a working connection when prepare() takes longer than that whole budget
FACTORY-702: prepare() runs an agent's multiple MCP servers CONCURRENTLY, not serially — worst case is the slowest ONE server, not their sum
FACTORY-702 review round 1: a connection that EXISTS but is NOT YET ready (its own proxy.ready still pending) is HELD, never forwarded straight into the proxy's own not-ready passthrough
FACTORY-702 review round 1: a request arriving BEFORE prepare() has even been INVOKED for this agent is still HELD, not failed fast, once prepare() starts and finishes within the hold window
integration: a daemon restart (new ResourceConnections, same workspace dir) answers 503 — never 401 — until prepare() runs again, then 200
policy "none" hands the spec back untouched and never touches the manager

FACTORY-75: builds a SpawnSpec carrying the modelPower/effort-resolved model+effort, not tierToModel
BUTCHR-453/BUTCHR-463: carries the definition's own strictMcpConfig through to the SpawnSpec

DROVR-42/FACTORY-67: for vendor claude, lizardMode is deliberately NEVER carried into the SpawnSpec — it never reaches the launched process's argv, unlike permissionMode/strictMcpConfig, so there is nothing for a stale-argv check to compare

FACTORY-108: for vendor codex, lizardMode IS carried into the SpawnSpec — the opposite of the claude case above — so agentLaunchConfig's Codex branch (src/agents/argv.ts) can drop --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox; absent/false forwards nothing, same as every other vendor's absent field
carries the definition's own mcpServers through to the SpawnSpec (BUTCHR-408, type ported from S4)
specForSessionDefinitionUnit dispatches resource units; a query-kind unit (never actually produced) throws rather than silently mis-spawning
recognises only the managed-sessions rule's own filesystem agent keys
one unit per eligible definition; frozen/invalid never appear
PR #394 review fix 1: `roles` is cleared and rebuilt every search from each eligible match's OWN manifest role, keyed by agent key — a frozen/removed definition's role does not linger
BUTCHR-460: `accountPolicies` is cleared and rebuilt every search from each eligible match's OWN manifest account policy, keyed by agent key — a frozen/removed definition's policy does not linger
FACTORY-75: `resolvedAgents` is cleared and rebuilt every search from each eligible match's OWN effectiveAgent() — a frozen/removed definition's entry does not linger

FACTORY-138/FACTORY-108/FACTORY-106 (DROVR-42/FACTORY-67 lineage): `lizardModes` is cleared and rebuilt every search from each eligible match's OWN manifest lizardMode, keyed by agent key — a vendor:claude definition defaults to ELIGIBLE (true) when absent (only explicit false opts out); a vendor:codex definition defaults to NOT eligible (false) when absent (the opposite default, a deliberate story decision — codex CAN set the field, unlike the claude default flip, but its own launch only drops the bypass flag on an explicit true, so default-eligible would only add a scan that can never find anything to press) — only an explicit true resolves eligible for codex, and explicit false stays not-eligible same as absent; a frozen/removed definition's entry does not linger

PR #394 review fix 1, end-to-end: a sentinel definition's agent is admitted and not counted against the cap, and a worker definition's agent is capped — through the REAL createAdmissionController, not a stub
activation is always active for whatever reaches it (frozen/invalid never do)
unchanged content never notifies; a size/mtime move notifies the resource's own agent only
brief content move: delivers with { definitionField: { brief: <new> } }, workingDirectory absent from the reason
workingDirectory content move: delivers with { definitionField: { workingDirectory: <new> } }, brief absent from the reason
both brief and workingDirectory move in the same poll: both keys present in the one reason
a non-brief/workingDirectory field move (e.g. vendor) still delivers with no reason — unchanged from before this ticket

check: true for the exact live token

only one-deep workspaces under the root are legacy
no rule loop owns a legacy agent, which is why startup must refuse
passes with only rule-engine agents, or none
a live legacy agent fails startup, naming it, its pane and the fix
a failed agent list fails closed rather than reading as none running
migration: only lists — no stop, no close, and legacy workspace files survive
working, idle, working => no stop: a single idle poll sandwiched between working polls is a flicker, not a stop
working, idle, idle => exactly one stop, reported on the 2nd confirming poll, anchored to the ORIGINAL working instant
dedup still holds after confirmation: further idle/none polls report nothing
working -> none confirms exactly like idle (the session is simply gone)
blocked counts as active: working -> blocked -> working never reports a stop
blocked counts as active: a working -> blocked -> idle,idle run's episode starts from when WORKING began, not from when blocked ended
resuming after a reported stop starts a fresh episode, and a later stop reports again
a ticket only ever observed idle/none never reports a stop (it was never active)
forget drops tracking so a later respawn starts a fresh episode
DoD 1: a stop with no self-tagged comment produces exactly one `[silent-stop] would flag KEY` line
DoD 1: a stop preceded by this ticket's own tagged comment produces no line
a comment tagged with a DIFFERENT key (a boss's tell_worker, or a peer's note) does NOT count as the worker having spoken
daemon chatter ([butchr:...]) does NOT count as the worker having spoken
a self-tagged comment landing BEFORE the current episode started does not count (it's old news)
DoD 2: dedup — a stop that stays idle across many polls logs only once
an unparseable comment `created` field fails toward NOT flagging
a failed comments fetch never flags — a declined check is not a confirmed silence
DoD 3: a stop within the suppression window of daemon start is suppressed, not flagged
DoD 3: a stop AFTER the suppression window has elapsed since daemon start is evaluated normally
DoD 3: a gap in polling far larger than the daemon's own cadence (a herdr reconnect) re-arms the suppression window
suppression is per-check-instance global, not per-issue: a reconnect suppresses every ticket's next stop, not just the one that happened to notice the gap
the pr-open context is included verbatim and never gates flag/no-flag
